name: Basilica of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary
history: Southampton's wealthy Protestant summer families largely paid for this church because their Irish Catholic household staff would not come east for the summer without a place to attend Mass. The cornerstone was laid on 28 July 1907 and the first Mass was said in 1908. Benedict XVI named it a basilica in 2011.
arch: Gothic Revival, clad in white marble and built partly with granite salvaged from the construction of the New York Public Library, for about $100,000. A square tower stands at the front corner.
features: Its stained glass windows and mosaic Stations of the Cross came from Innsbruck, Austria.
Shamrock motifs in the stone arches honour the Irish servants for whom it was built.

look.d: Its four bells were cast in Troy, New York, and weathered a century of salt air.
Founded so Irish household workers could keep the Sunday Mass.

fun: Some of its stone came from the New York Public Library's construction.
journal: A Hamptons basilica built for the cooks and maids. Shamrocks hidden in the stone.

a: So Irish household staff could attend Mass in summer

quiz.q: Where were the stained glass windows made?
